messages:
jia_localization: Heads-up — during atlas-v2 int4 onboarding I hit a weird localized regression on the vertical-Japanese + inline Arabic transliteration set. BLEU dropped ~6pt vs fp16.
li-wei: :eyes: can you paste the repro and a minimal example? is this only int4 or also q8?
jia_localization: Quick repro below (full harness in the artifact link). Only happens on int4 (q8 and fp16 look fine). ran on staging cpu/gpu.
--- eval command ---
./eval/run_mt_eval.sh --model atlas-v2-int4 --dataset vertical_jp_arab_translit --split test --batch 8
# output
BLEU: 21.4 (-6.1)
chrF: 48.2 (-3.4)

Sample input (vertical layout, ruby annotations inline):
【垂直】
漢字【かんじ】/كلمة‎

Expected (fp16):
漢字（かんじ）/كلمة — translated fluent line

Atlas-v2-int4 output:
漢字/ か ん じ /كلمة‎ — extra spaces, rubies detached, translit stitched into prior token causing misalignment
eli_research: hm looks like token boundaries move when ZWJ/vertical markers present. did you check tokenization mapping between fp16 and int4 artifacts? sometimes quant kernels change sentencepiece fallback.
tanner_infra: can you dump the token ids for both runs? also confirm cache behavior — prefix-KV cache might get reused incorrectly if tokenization changes subtlely.

jia_localization: dumped tokens — here's a small snippet (fp16 vs int4):
fp16 tokens: [1245, 78, 9003, 11, 432]
int4 tokens: [1245, 78, 900, 3, 11, 432]
(note the extra split at 900 -> 900,3)

li-wei: that split would definitely shift alignment. could be tokenizer rounding/normalization preproc difference in the quantized transform? are we applying the same normalization pipeline before tokenization in the int4 path?

jia_localization: pipeline is identical per config, but the int4 loader uses a slightly different Python binding in the runtime (C++ token piece fallback of tokeniser). suspecting a kernel-induced encoding of ZWJ/vertical marker bytes.

nora_evalbot: added the failing examples to the regression dashboard: https://dash.internal/regressions/2678901234

eli_research: two hypotheses:
1) tokenizer normalization bug in the int4 runtime path (string normalization or unicode NFKC/NFC differences)
2) model learned subtokenization shift when quantized (rare but possible with fake-quant or calibration mismatch)

tanner_infra: try forcing explicit unicode normalization at preprocessing to NFC and re-run. if that fixes it, it's a pre-tokenizer difference and we can patch quickly.

jia_localization: quick patch test result — forced NFC on input and reran one epoch of eval:
BLEU: 26.9 (-0.6)
chrF: 51.0 (-0.6)
So most of the delta goes away.

li-wei: interesting — that points to normalization. can you provide the raw bytes (hex) around the boundary for one failing example? I'll check the tokenizer fallback C++ binding.

jia_localization: raw bytes attached (pasted): 0xE3 0x80 0x90 0xE6 0xBC 0xA2 0xE5 0xAD 0x97 0xE3 0x80 0x91 0x5B 0xD8 0xA3 ... — the ZWJ/vertical brackets mixed with Arabic mark sequences.

eli_research: we should also audit the quant calibration runner. If calibration used a slightly different byte-level input (e.g., trimmed/normalized sample) the int4 lookup table could be skewed for those rare grapheme clusters.

nora_evalbot: created ticket ML-5847 and attached failing inputs + token dumps.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: created ephemeral job atlas-v2-int4-tokenizer-check-2678901234 (logs: https://ci.internal/jobs/atlas-v2-int4-tokenizer-check-2678901234)

li-wei: plan: 1) bisect the runtime binding commit that changed tokenization behavior 2) add NFC normalization as safe fallback in preprocessing 3) rerun calibration with normalized corpus and compare. I'll take 1.

jia_localization: thanks — putting the failing subset into a canary that goes to Dedicated staging with forced NFC by default until we confirm. will update ticket with artifacts.

eli_research: long-term we should add an automated smoke that runs a small vertical/ruby/RTL suite on quant builds. put it in the model onboarding checklist.

li-wei: agreed. adding to onboarding checklist: "run unicode-normalization-sensitive SMT suite".

tanner_infra: if we push the preprocessing change, let's do it as an opt-in flag first and roll across models after regression window.

jia_localization: noted. ping me if you want the test vectors.

li-wei: grabbing vectors now, will start bisecting commit range.

jia_localization: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
